primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Selective targeting of proteins for ubiquitin-dependent degradation by E3 ubiquitin ligases
mechanism: In the ubiquitin-proteasome system, E1 activates ubiquitin, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 ubiquitin ligases provide much of the substrate specificity by recognizing target proteins and promoting ubiquitin transfer. Polyubiquitinated substrates can then be recognized and degraded by the proteasome.
vignette: A researcher studies a short-lived cell-cycle regulatory protein. Ubiquitin activation and transfer to E2 enzymes remain intact, but a mutation prevents recognition of this specific target protein; the target is no longer efficiently polyubiquitinated and accumulates in the cell.
lead: Loss of function of which component most directly explains the selective failure to recognize this substrate?
distractor_notes: E1 activates ubiquitin globally and does not provide the principal target-specific recognition described in the stem.
The proteasome degrades already ubiquitinated substrates; the defect here occurs before polyubiquitination because the target is not recognized.
Deubiquitinating enzymes remove ubiquitin from substrates and do not account for the primary selective recognition step required to tag this protein.
Lysosomal hydrolases mediate lysosomal degradation rather than selective substrate recognition in the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
key_expl: E3 ubiquitin ligases bind specific substrate proteins and confer much of the selectivity of the ubiquitination system. E1 and E2 handle ubiquitin activation/transfer, whereas E3 determines which target is efficiently ubiquitinated.
objective: Identify E3 ubiquitin ligases as the principal substrate-recognition components that confer specificity to ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Bile-salt mixed micelles facilitate transport of lipid-digestion products to the intestinal brush border
mechanism: Conjugated bile salts are amphipathic molecules that emulsify dietary lipids and form mixed micelles containing fatty acids, monoglycerides, cholesterol, and fat-soluble vitamins. Micelles keep hydrophobic digestion products soluble in the aqueous intestinal lumen and deliver them to the enterocyte brush border for absorption.
vignette: A patient with severe depletion of the intestinal bile-salt pool has normal pancreatic lipase secretion. Triglycerides are hydrolyzed in the lumen, but uptake of long-chain fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins across the small-intestinal mucosa is markedly reduced.
lead: Which process is most directly impaired?
correct: Formation of mixed micelles that transport hydrophobic lipids to the enterocyte brush border
distractors: Hydrolysis of triglycerides by pancreatic lipase
Re-esterification of fatty acids to triglycerides inside enterocytes
Assembly of chylomicrons around apolipoprotein B-48
Exocytosis of chylomicrons into intestinal lymphatics
distractor_notes: Pancreatic lipase secretion is stated to be normal and triglyceride hydrolysis is occurring; the defect is downstream luminal solubilization/transport.
Re-esterification occurs after lipid products enter the enterocyte and therefore cannot explain impaired delivery from the aqueous lumen to the brush border.
Chylomicron assembly occurs intracellularly after absorption; bile-salt depletion primarily impairs micellar delivery of hydrophobic lipids before entry.
Lymphatic exocytosis occurs after intracellular lipid processing and chylomicron assembly, not during luminal micellar transport.
key_expl: Bile salts form amphipathic mixed micelles that solubilize lipid-digestion products in the intestinal lumen and bring them to the brush border. Lipase can remain functional while absorption still fails when the bile-salt pool is severely depleted.
objective: Explain how bile-salt mixed micelles enable absorption of long-chain lipids and fat-soluble vitamins by delivering them through the aqueous intestinal lumen to the brush border.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Dorsal column-medial lemniscus fibers decussate as internal arcuate fibers in the caudal medulla
mechanism: Primary afferents carrying vibration, fine touch and proprioception ascend ipsilaterally in fasciculi gracilis/cuneatus and synapse in the gracile/cuneate nuclei of the caudal medulla. Second-order axons cross the midline as internal arcuate fibers and then ascend contralaterally as the medial lemniscus.
vignette: A focal lesion damages second-order axons immediately after they leave the nucleus gracilis but before they join the medial lemniscus. The affected pathway carries vibration and conscious proprioception from the lower limb.
lead: At which location are these axons crossing the midline?
correct: Caudal medulla as internal arcuate fibers
distractors: Anterior white commissure of the spinal cord
Posterior limb of the internal capsule
distractor_notes: Pain and temperature fibers of the spinothalamic pathway cross in the anterior white commissure, not dorsal-column modalities.
The posterior limb carries already-crossed thalamocortical somatosensory fibers and is not the site of dorsal-column decussation.
The tectum is not the decussation site of gracile/cuneate second-order neurons.
By the pons, medial lemniscus fibers have already crossed in the caudal medulla.
key_expl: Second-order neurons from the gracile and cuneate nuclei decussate in the caudal medulla as internal arcuate fibers. After crossing, they ascend as the medial lemniscus.
objective: Localize the sensory decussation of the dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway to internal arcuate fibers in the caudal medulla.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Osteoprotegerin inhibits osteoclastogenesis by acting as a decoy receptor for RANKL
mechanism: RANKL expressed by osteoblast-lineage/stromal cells binds RANK on osteoclast precursors and promotes osteoclast differentiation and activation. Osteoprotegerin (OPG), produced by osteoblasts/stromal cells, binds RANKL as a soluble decoy receptor and prevents RANK activation, thereby suppressing osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption.
vignette: Cultured osteoblast-lineage cells are engineered to secrete large amounts of a soluble protein that binds RANK ligand before it can interact with receptors on osteoclast precursors. Osteoclast formation and bone resorption decrease.
lead: Which protein was most likely overexpressed?
distractor_notes: RANK is the receptor on osteoclast precursors; increased RANK availability would support rather than neutralize RANKL signaling.
M-CSF promotes survival/proliferation of osteoclast precursors and does not act as a soluble RANKL decoy receptor.
PTHrP can increase bone resorption indirectly through osteoblast-lineage signaling and does not sequester RANKL.
Cathepsin K is an osteoclast protease involved in matrix degradation after osteoclast differentiation, not the extracellular decoy receptor.
key_expl: Osteoprotegerin binds RANKL and prevents it from activating RANK on osteoclast precursors. This decreases osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption.
objective: Identify osteoprotegerin as the soluble decoy receptor that inhibits RANKL-RANK signaling and osteoclast differentiation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Positive renal free-water clearance during excretion of urine hypotonic to plasma
mechanism: Free-water clearance is the portion of urine flow representing solute-free water excretion and is defined as CH2O = V − Cosm = V(1 − Uosm/Posm). When urine osmolality is lower than plasma osmolality, free-water clearance is positive; when urine is hypertonic to plasma, it is negative.
vignette: After a large oral water load, a healthy adult suppresses vasopressin release. Urine flow is 6 mL/min, urine osmolality is 100 mOsm/kg, and plasma osmolality is 300 mOsm/kg.
lead: Which statement about this patient's renal water handling is correct?
correct: Free-water clearance is positive because urine is hypotonic to plasma
distractors: Free-water clearance is negative because urine flow is high
Free-water clearance is zero because total solute excretion is unchanged
Osmolar clearance must exceed total urine flow
Positive free-water clearance indicates net renal water retention
distractor_notes: The sign of free-water clearance depends on urine osmolality relative to plasma, not simply the urine flow rate; hypotonic urine gives positive clearance.
Free-water clearance is zero only when urine is isosmotic with plasma.
When urine is dilute, osmolar clearance is smaller than total urine flow, leaving a positive free-water component.
Positive free-water clearance means the kidney is excreting water in excess of that required to excrete solute isosmotically.
key_expl: Because Uosm is below Posm, the kidney is excreting hypotonic urine. CH2O = V(1 − Uosm/Posm) is therefore positive; with the values given it would be 4 mL/min, representing net solute-free water excretion.
objective: Interpret free-water clearance from the relationship between urine and plasma osmolality and recognize that dilute urine produces positive free-water clearance.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Tonic inhibition of prolactin secretion by hypothalamic dopamine acting at lactotroph D2 receptors
mechanism: Unlike most anterior-pituitary hormones, prolactin is under dominant tonic inhibitory control from hypothalamic tuberoinfundibular dopamine. Dopamine reaches lactotrophs through portal blood and activates D2 receptors, reducing prolactin synthesis and secretion; dopamine antagonism or pituitary-stalk disruption removes this inhibition and raises prolactin.
vignette: A pituitary cell culture contains normal lactotrophs. Addition of a hypothalamic neurotransmitter rapidly decreases prolactin release. This effect is abolished by a selective dopamine-receptor antagonist.
lead: Which receptor on lactotrophs mediates the physiologic inhibitory signal?
distractor_notes: D1 receptors are not the principal lactotroph receptor mediating tonic dopaminergic suppression of prolactin.
TRH can stimulate prolactin secretion rather than mediate the dominant inhibitory pathway.
GnRH receptors regulate gonadotroph secretion of LH and FSH, not tonic prolactin inhibition.
GHRH receptors regulate somatotroph growth-hormone secretion.
key_expl: Hypothalamic dopamine is the principal tonic inhibitor of prolactin secretion. It acts on D2 receptors on anterior-pituitary lactotrophs; D2 blockade or interruption of dopamine delivery causes hyperprolactinemia.
objective: Identify lactotroph D2 receptors as the target of tonic hypothalamic dopaminergic inhibition of prolactin secretion.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Thin basement membrane nephropathy is a type IV collagen disorder, commonly associated with heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants. It typically causes persistent or intermittent isolated microscopic hematuria with relatively preserved kidney function and no characteristic hearing or ocular abnormalities. Electron microscopy shows diffuse uniform thinning of the glomerular basement membrane.
vignette: A 22-year-old woman is evaluated for persistent microscopic hematuria found on routine examinations since childhood. Blood pressure, serum creatinine, and urine protein are normal. Her mother also has isolated microscopic hematuria. Hearing and ophthalmologic examinations are normal. Electron microscopy of a renal biopsy shows diffuse uniform thinning of the glomerular basement membrane without lamellation or splitting.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractor_notes: Alport syndrome can involve type IV collagen but more often has progressive renal disease and may include sensorineural hearing or ocular abnormalities; electron microscopy typically shows irregular splitting/lamellation rather than uniform thinning.
IgA nephropathy often produces episodic gross hematuria associated with mucosal infections and mesangial IgA deposition rather than diffuse uniform GBM thinning.
Poststreptococcal disease presents acutely after infection with nephritic features and immune-complex findings rather than lifelong familial isolated hematuria.
Membranous nephropathy classically causes nephrotic-range proteinuria and subepithelial immune deposits, not isolated microscopic hematuria with a thin GBM.
key_expl: Familial isolated microscopic hematuria with preserved kidney function, absent extrarenal Alport features, and diffuse uniform GBM thinning is characteristic of thin basement membrane nephropathy, often related to heterozygous COL4A3/COL4A4 variants.
objective: Recognize thin basement membrane nephropathy from familial isolated microscopic hematuria and diffuse uniform thinning of the glomerular basement membrane.

outline: Slow oxidative versus fast glycolytic fibers
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Type I slow oxidative skeletal-muscle fibers are adapted for sustained endurance activity
mechanism: Type I fibers are slow oxidative fibers with abundant mitochondria, capillary supply and myoglobin, relatively low myosin ATPase activity, slow contraction and high fatigue resistance. Fast glycolytic type II fibers have higher myosin ATPase activity, fewer mitochondria/myoglobin, rely more on anaerobic glycolysis and fatigue more rapidly.
vignette: A biopsy is obtained from a muscle used continuously to maintain posture. One fiber population has high mitochondrial density, abundant myoglobin, rich capillary supply, low myosin ATPase activity, and marked resistance to fatigue.
lead: Which fiber type is being described?
distractors: Type II fibers with low mitochondrial density and high fatigability
distractor_notes: Fast glycolytic fibers have higher myosin ATPase activity, lower mitochondrial/myoglobin content and greater fatigability.
This description explicitly states the opposite metabolic and fatigue profile from the biopsy.
Denervation causes pathologic atrophy and fiber-type grouping rather than a normal endurance-adapted oxidative phenotype.
Purkinje fibers are specialized cardiac conduction cells and are not skeletal-muscle contractile fiber types.
key_expl: Type I slow oxidative fibers are rich in mitochondria, myoglobin and capillaries, contract relatively slowly, have low myosin ATPase activity and resist fatigue, making them well suited for posture and endurance.
objective: Differentiate type I slow oxidative skeletal-muscle fibers from faster glycolytic fiber types using metabolic, structural and functional characteristics.

diagnosis: False discovery rate control is appropriate when many hypotheses are tested and some false positives among declared discoveries are acceptable
mechanism: The false discovery rate is the expected proportion of false positives among hypotheses declared significant. The Benjamini-Hochberg step-up procedure controls FDR and generally retains greater power than procedures such as Bonferroni correction that control the family-wise probability of any false-positive result.
vignette: Investigators test 20,000 gene-expression associations in an exploratory study. They expect that some true associations exist and want to limit the expected proportion of false positives among the results they declare significant, while preserving more power than a Bonferroni correction.
lead: Which statistical approach best matches this goal?
correct: Control the false discovery rate with a Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
distractors: Use an unadjusted P < .05 threshold for every comparison
Apply a Bonferroni correction to control the probability of any family-wise type I error
Increase the sample size without adjusting for multiple testing
Report only associations with the largest effect size regardless of P value
distractor_notes: With thousands of tests, unadjusted thresholds produce excessive false-positive discoveries.
Bonferroni controls family-wise error and is generally more conservative; the stated goal specifically targets the proportion of false discoveries while retaining power.
Larger samples improve precision/power but do not by themselves solve multiplicity-induced false-positive inflation.
Effect size alone does not provide formal control of the expected false-positive proportion among reported discoveries.
key_expl: FDR control targets the expected proportion of false positives among declared discoveries. Benjamini-Hochberg is designed for this setting and is usually less conservative than family-wise methods such as Bonferroni.
objective: Distinguish false-discovery-rate control from family-wise error control and identify Benjamini-Hochberg as an appropriate method for large-scale multiple testing.
clues: limit proportion of false positives among discoveries

system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
diagnosis: Collaborative agenda setting at the start of a visit with multiple patient concerns
mechanism: Effective agenda setting begins by eliciting the patient's full list of concerns before diving deeply into one issue, adding clinician priorities, then collaboratively prioritizing what can be addressed during the current visit and arranging follow-up for remaining concerns. This reduces late-emerging 'doorknob' concerns and supports patient-centered communication.
vignette: At the start of a 20-minute primary-care visit, a patient says, “My knee has been hurting, and I also want to talk about my headaches, poor sleep, and whether I need a colonoscopy.” None of the concerns appears immediately life-threatening.
lead: Which response best demonstrates effective agenda setting?
correct: “I want to make sure we know everything you hoped to discuss. Is there something else? Then we can decide together which concerns are most important to address today and make a plan for the rest.”
distractors: “Let's start with the knee pain now, and we can see at the end whether there is time for anything else.”
“You have too many concerns for one visit, so choose one before we discuss anything further.”
“I will decide which problem is most medically important and address only that issue today.”
“We should schedule separate visits for every concern before discussing any of them.”
distractor_notes: Diving immediately into the first complaint risks missing other priorities and late-emerging concerns; effective agenda setting first elicits the full concern list.
Patients should help prioritize concerns, but the clinician should first elicit the complete agenda and negotiate priorities collaboratively rather than force a choice without discussion.
Clinician safety priorities matter, but nonurgent visits should use shared agenda setting rather than unilateral selection.
Some concerns may require follow-up visits, but the agenda should first be elicited and prioritized rather than refusing to address any issue now.
key_expl: The best approach is to elicit the complete concern list early, add clinician priorities, and negotiate a shared, realistic agenda for the current visit with follow-up for unresolved issues.
objective: Use collaborative agenda setting to elicit all patient concerns early and jointly prioritize what can be addressed during a time-limited clinical encounter.
